title: A Key Bridge to Crimea Is Badly Damaged
summary: Ukraine says it has severely damaged a critical bridge linking Russia to Crimea, in what President Volodymyr Zelensky called an unprecedented operation weeks in the making. Video footage appeared to show a large arched section of the bridge's road deck destroyed, with pieces of the support arch and roadway jutting out of the water below. Zelensky said the overnight strike was the result of a seven-stage operation by Ukraine's military and security services, which gradually knocked out air defence systems, radars and electronic warfare equipment on the way to the final target. He said the rail section beside the road had also been hit by a wave of drones, although its supporting arch was still standing and a Russian-backed official said some rail services were still running. The bridge matters because it carries both road and rail traffic for Russian soldiers heading toward the front line. It was built by Russia after it annexed the Crimean peninsula in 2014 and was opened by Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2018. Ukraine has targeted it before but has struggled to close it for good. The Kremlin insisted the bridge would be rebuilt better than before. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said it would be restored following the strikes, and Russia's Investigative Committee confirmed structural damage and said it had opened a criminal case. The timing is significant: the strike came just before Putin was due to meet the leaders of China and the United States in Shenzhen on Thursday. Meanwhile, Kyiv's mayor said two important bridges over the Dnipro River in the Ukrainian capital were closed after Russia targeted the city overnight, disrupting heating and water. Russia's defence ministry said it had downed 2,256 drones, the biggest Ukrainian drone attack since the war began, for the second day in a row.
why_it_matters: The bridge is a key supply route in the war, so its damage could change how the fighting develops and what leaders discuss at their meeting.

background_read: Crimea is a peninsula, a piece of land almost surrounded by water, on the Black Sea.
Russia took control of it in 2014 and built a bridge to connect it to Russia.
The bridge carries both road traffic and trains, including supplies for soldiers.
Bridges like this are important in wartime because armies use them to move people and supplies.
